name: Mobian
summary: Mobile overlay for Debian GNU/Linux providing a Wayland touch environment and telephony tools on smartphones and tablets.
license: Open source (GPL, LGPL and free Debian licences)

content.introduction: Mobian is a community project created in 2020 by Arnaud Ferraris whose objective is to adapt the universal Debian GNU/Linux distribution for use on mobile devices, notably smartphones and touch tablets.
content.what_is_it: Rather than an autonomous and independent derived distribution, Mobian works as an overlay on top of Debian. The project maintains a limited number of specific packages while systematically feeding the upstream code ("upstreaming") into the official Debian repositories through the DebianOnMobile team.
content.origine_et_premieres_versions_stables:
Mobian has followed the Debian *testing* repository since its origin, and not the stable versions. The first stable version of the project, named "Bookworm", was published on 10 June 2023, at the same time as Debian Bookworm: the announcement specifies that Debian Bullseye had not been judged suitable for mobile devices and that Bookworm is the first Debian version considered usable enough on a touch screen to serve as the basis for a stable version of Mobian. From this publication onwards, users can choose between this stable version and the *staging* repository, which follows the development branch.

The retrospective published in January 2024 specifies the maintenance policy of that branch: Bookworm continues to receive security updates, but no new features; developments are made in the *testing* repositories of Debian and of Mobian.
content.debian_foundation_and_mobile_overlay: Mobian relies directly on the stable and testing repositories of Debian (Debian 12 Bookworm, Debian 13 Trixie). The system uses the standard glibc library, the systemd service and init manager, as well as the APT binary package manager (dpkg). Users thus have native access to the whole Debian catalogue, with more than 69,000 software packages. The root file system remains modifiable in read-write mode by default, allowing standard system administration of a Debian machine.
content.touch_environment_and_phosh_ecosystem: Mobian's main graphical environment is Phosh (Phone Shell), a touch interface designed for mobile terminals above the wlroots Wayland compositor, initially developed by Purism for the Librem 5 and today hosted under the aegis of GNOME. Phosh is associated with Squeekboard, an on-screen virtual keyboard handling the multi-language layout and modifier keys, and with Feedbackd, a system daemon orchestrating haptic (vibration) and sound signals. Cellular telephony, SMS sending and mobile data management are ensured by ModemManager and NetworkManager, while the audio routing of telephone conversations is handled by Callaudiod and PipeWire, making it possible to run adaptive GNOME desktop applications using the libadwaita and libhandy libraries.
content.hardware_support_and_mainline_kernel: Mobian applies a strict technical policy: the system relies exclusively on the upstream Linux kernel ("mainline kernel") and refuses the use of modified Android kernels or proprietary bootloaders. This orientation deliberately limits the catalogue of supported hardware to devices whose architecture is documented and supported by the official Linux kernel: mainly the PinePhone and the PinePhone Pro from Pine64, the Librem 5 from Purism, as well as certain x86-64 tablets and experimental single-board computers. Mobian follows the continuous development cycle of Debian Testing (currently Trixie), the mobile-specific packages being progressively backported and integrated directly into the official repositories of the upstream Debian project.
content.technical_constraints_and_hardware_limit: The uncompromising adoption of the mainline Linux kernel generates significant practical constraints for the end user. Battery life remains noticeably lower than that of a conventional Android system, although deep sleep management (suspend-to-RAM through the Crust firmware on the Allwinner A64 architecture) makes it possible to reach several hours of inactivity while preserving the reception of incoming calls and SMS. Hardware acceleration of camera sensors requires specific image processing modules (such as Megapixels), and the application ecosystem is that of GNU/Linux desktop free software, excluding direct access to banking applications or to proprietary mobile services requiring the Android SafetyNet or Play Integrity certifications.
content.images_and_installation: Mobian images are published on images.mobian.org. Installation follows the procedure described on the page of each device in the list of supported devices; the project's Debian documentation additionally lists the known problems and software limitations, as well as procedures for common tasks. Plasma Mobile can be used instead of Phosh on a Mobian installation, and Debian provides the corresponding package.
content.debian_release_tracking_and_signed_archi: Mobian follows Debian's stable releases. Its current stable was announced on 13 October 2025, about two months after the Debian release, with images built on Phosh 46.0 and Plasma Mobile 6.3 running a 6.12 kernel for almost all supported devices (the Librem 5 remains on 6.6). Stable images are published for the PinePhone, PinePhone Pro, PineTab, Librem 5, Pixel 3a and 3a XL, OnePlus 6 and 6T, and Pocophone F1; images also exist for the Fairphone 4 and 5, the PineTab 2 and the SHIFT6mq, with the project stating that important hardware features such as Wi-Fi or audio do not work on those. Images and the package archive are signed with PGP keys that were rotated at this transition, the previous key having expired since the preceding stable; the project recommends backing up data and flashing a fresh image rather than upgrading in place, and documents the manual upgrade path for users who attempt it.
content.avis_de_securite_et_traitement_des_corre:
On 31 August 2023, the Mobian team published its first security advisory. The Bookworm images published earlier in the year contained a small number of files with world-writable permissions; two of them being used for the configuration of the APT package manager, they offered a local privilege escalation method: a local user could obtain root access by modifying these files and then waiting for the installation of an update supplied by the attacker. The advisory specifies that the attack requires an unlocked or already compromised device and that no remote path exists.

The fix is delivered by the `mobian-tweaks-common` package, in version 0.5.6+deb12u1 for Bookworm and 0.5.9 for Trixie and staging; it installs a script that corrects the permissions of the files concerned. The update goes through the normal procedure, `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade`, or through GNOME Software; the packages are published in the `staging` and `bookworm-updates` repositories before migration to `trixie` and `bookworm`. The advisory provides two indicators of compromise: the file `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/mobian.list` must contain the line `deb http://repo.mobian.org/ <distribution> main non-free-firmware`, and `/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/mobian.gpg` can be verified by SHA-256 fingerprint. The problem was reported by a user credited under the pseudonym @Ove.
content.advantages: Mobian offers the complete Debian ecosystem on a mobile terminal, continuous integration into the upstream repositories avoiding fragmentation, a standard read-write system administrable through APT, and total independence from the commercial services of Google and Apple.
content.disadvantages: Battery life in standby and thermal management are less optimised than under commercial Android systems, camera sensor drivers remain limited, and the catalogue of native purely touch applications is reduced compared with the dominant mobile platforms.
content.who_is_it_for: Mobian addresses system administrators, developers and advanced Linux users wishing to find a standard and verifiable Debian environment on their compatible smartphone or tablet.
content.who_is_it_not_for: Mobian is not suited to users looking for a turnkey mainstream experience, a battery life of several days without configuration, or guaranteed access to banking applications and mobile games requiring the DRM and SafetyNet certifications of Google.
content.verdict: Mobian constitutes a rigorous gateway between the Debian ecosystem and mobile computing, offering an authentic GNU/Linux platform on a mainline kernel while accepting the compromises inherent to mobile hardware not specifically designed for free drivers.

relations.name: Debian
relations.note: Parent distribution providing the whole set of binary package repositories, upstream governance and build infrastructure for Mobian.

relations.name: Nura
relations.note: Mobile Linux distribution based on Alpine Linux sharing with Mobian the mainline kernel target and the Wayland touch interfaces.

relations.name: PureOS
relations.note: Debian-based operating system developed by Purism, at the origin of the initial development of the Phosh touch shell.

relations.name: Ubuntu Touch
relations.note: Alternative free mobile distribution maintained by UBports, using the convergent Lomiri graphical environment.
